cards.name: Focus
cards.description: 1 Spirit. If your stamina < opponent, discard all Focus for redraw (max 3 reloads per turn).

rulebook.title: Fractured Fist
rulebook.intro: Two fighters, two decks. Each turn you play techniques to queue damage and defense, then spend spirit to buy better cards. When both of you have had a turn, the blows land at the same time. Bring your opponent's stamina to 0.

win.title: Bring their stamina to 0
win.text: Each player starts with the same stamina. Damage lands in the strike at the end of each round. A player at 0 stamina or less loses.
win.tie: If both players reach 0 in the same strike, the game is a tie.

components.intro: Each player has their own copy of everything below. Nothing is shared, not even the cards you buy from.

items.name: Focus
items.text: 7 in your starting deck and 20 in your supply. Worth 1 spirit.

items.name: Missteps
items.text: 3 in your starting deck. Keep the rest within reach: your opponent can push more into your discard pile.

items.name: Technique cards
items.text: 5 copies of each of the game's 7 techniques, one pile per card.

items.name: Stamina tracker
items.text: A die, a dial or a counter.

components.note: You can never hold more than 10 Missteps across your deck, hand and discard pile. Missteps sent past that are not added.

steps: Choose the 7 techniques for this game. Both players use the same ones. For a first game, use the starter set shown below.
Each player makes their own supply: 5 copies of each technique, and 20 each of Focus, Momentum and Mastery.
Each player shuffles a starting deck of 7 Focus and 3 Missteps, then draws a hand of 5.
Choose who goes first. That order stays for the whole game.
setup.deck_caption: Your starting deck: 7 Focus and 3 Missteps.
setup.loadout_caption: The starter set. Between them they do everything: Attack, Block, Assess, Center, Distract, Quicken, React.

round.intro: In each round, both players take one turn, in seat order. Then the strike settles the round.

turn.name: Technique
turn.text: Play technique cards. Each one uses 1 action, and you start with 1.

turn.name: Channel
turn.text: Play resource cards for spirit. Spend it to buy cards into your discard pile.

turn.name: Cleanup
turn.text: Discard the rest of your hand and draw 5 new cards.

strike.name: Strike
strike.text: Both players' damage and defense land at the same time.

round.note: You can skip the Channel phase by ending your turn straight from the Technique phase. You can't go back to the Technique phase once you are channeling.

technique.intro: You start each turn with 1 action. Playing a technique uses 1 action, and its effects happen right away, in the order you play. A card that gives more Tech lets you play more techniques this turn. Played cards stay face up in front of you until the strike. A card's cost is only what it takes to buy it.

example.title: Example: one action becomes three

steps.text: Play React. It uses your 1 action and gives you 2 more.

example.close: With no actions left, move on to the Channel phase. The two Focus cards will pay for something there.

effects.intro: Every technique is a list of these effects, printed on the card.

list.text: Added to the damage you deal in this round's strike.
Taken off the damage your opponent deals you in this round's strike.
That many more actions this turn.
Draw that many cards right now.
That much spirit to spend in this turn's Channel phase.
You may buy that many more cards this turn.
Remove up to that many cards in your hand from the game, right now.
Put that many Missteps into your opponent's discard pile (never past 10).
Get back that much stamina, never above what you started with.

channel.intro: In the Channel phase, play resource cards for spirit. Spirit from techniques you played this turn adds to it. To buy a card, spend spirit equal to its cost; it goes into your discard pile. You may buy 1 card a turn, plus 1 more for each Channel effect you played. Leftover spirit can pay for another buy, and is lost when your turn ends.

example.title: Example: buying an Attack

steps.text: Move on to the Channel phase.
Buy Attack for 4. It goes into your discard pile, and that is your one buy this turn.

example.close: The Misstep and the Block are still in your hand. They are discarded at cleanup.

refine.intro: A card with Refine lets you remove up to that many cards in your hand from the game, one at a time. They are gone for good, not discarded. You must finish refining, or skip the rest, before you do anything else.
refine.missteps: Missteps do nothing and can never be played. Your starting deck has 3. Refining is the only way to get rid of them.

example.title: Example: clearing out two Missteps

steps.text: Remove a Misstep from the game.

example.close: Only 1 Misstep is left in your deck now, so your future hands are stronger.

reload.title: Focus reload: the catch-up rule
reload.text: If your stamina is lower than your opponent's, you may discard every Focus card in your hand and draw that many new cards. You may do this up to 3 times a turn, in either phase, but not while you still have refines to use.

steps: Discard the rest of your hand.
Draw 5 new cards. If your deck runs out, draw what is left, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck, and draw the rest.
The cards you played stay in front of you until the strike.

strike.intro: After both players have had a turn, both deal damage at the same time. You deal your damage minus your opponent's defense, never less than 0.

example.title: Example: both fighters land a blow
steps: You deal 3 − 2 = 1, so your opponent loses 1 stamina.
They deal 2 − 1 = 1, so you lose 1 stamina.
Had they queued 4 defense, you would deal 0, not a negative amount.

strike.end: Then every played card goes to its owner's discard pile, actions, buys and spirit reset, and the next round starts with the first player.

cards.intro: Every card in the game. Each game uses seven techniques; the resources and Missteps are always in play.

groups.title: Resources
groups.text: Played in the Channel phase for spirit.

groups.title: Misstep
groups.text: Can never be played. Refine it to remove it.

groups.title: The starter set
groups.text: One technique for each kind of effect.

groups.title: The Awakened
groups.text: Spirit and healing: last longer and buy more.

groups.title: Uncounted
groups.text: Fill the other player's deck with Missteps.
